context: a letter from Daniel Oliver, which you are answering
exchanges:
I have looked over Müller’s paper & return it by this post. It will be an interesting thing for an evening Meeting.— I have corrected his bracteæ, &—assisted by Mr Bentham—the haziness of the paragraph about upwards & downwards, &c. Dr. Hooker returns on Thursday— I have a note this morning. He does not lose the stiffness in his joints yet.—

The scrap of Strychnos cannot be named with any certainty. Young shoots are often so different from those on the flowering branch

Ever very sincerely yrs | D Oliver

I am extremely obliged to you for all the trouble you have taken in correcting so fully the paper which I sent you, & which I will now transmit to Linn. Soc.

Dear Oliver | yours very sincerely | Ch. Darwin
